summary: One-click managed local model experience for MetisNote. Users choose a model and click Add & Download; the app handles everything else. No IP address, port, protocol, or API key is ever shown to the user.
designPrinciples: One-click first: the normal path is a single primary action, not a form.
Zero-config by default: protocol, endpoint, port, runtime arguments, and model identifier are system-managed and never shown to the user.
Progressive disclosure: advanced runtime tuning is hidden unless the user explicitly asks for it.
Safe automation: preflight checks, checksum verification, health checks, and rollback happen automatically.
Single source of truth: installed artifacts, active runtime, and visible LLM configs are linked by internal IDs instead of manual strings.

userPromise.primaryAction: Choose a model and click "Add & Download".
normalUserNeedsToDo: Click the primary action button once.
systemWillDo: Choose the default verified quantization for the selected model.
Check disk space, memory expectations, platform, and runtime compatibility.
Download the GGUF model file and prepare the bundled node-llama-cpp runtime automatically.
Install the model into managed storage and keep runtime metadata under managed state.
Create a managed-local LLM config automatically.
Bind the internal runtime handle and request model name automatically (never shown to user).
Start the local runtime and mark the model ready when runtime initialization succeeds.
Enable the new local model automatically when there is no active local model yet.
hiddenFromUser: internal runtime route or compatibility endpoint
runtime backend details and launch parameters
model identifier (the model field in API requests)
API Key input (managed models do not need a key)

configTypes.summary: Managed-local is the primary path for local models; legacy self-hosted llama.cpp-style endpoints remain an advanced fallback concept only.

custom.purpose: User-defined remote models with custom endpoint.

llamacpp.purpose: Advanced option for users who run their own llama.cpp or compatible inference server externally.
llamacpp.userEntry: Generic model dialog, deprioritized under an advanced section.
llamacpp.notes: Not the default local model entry point. Intended for power users only.

managed-local.purpose: System-managed local model. The primary way for normal users to use local models.
managed-local.endpointSource: Derived by the runtime manager internally. Never user-editable. Never displayed.
managed-local.userEntry: Dedicated Local Models page only. Not created via the generic model dialog.
managed-local.editBehavior: Clicking edit in the generic model list redirects to the dedicated Local Models page.
managed-local.displayFormat: Show as 'Local Model · {displayName}' with status badge. No endpoint, port, or IP shown.

happyPath: User sees a short curated list of recommended local models rather than protocol or endpoint forms.
User clicks "Add & Download" on a model card or list row.
App runs preflight checks and shows a single inline progress card.
App downloads model artifacts, verifies them, installs them, and creates the managed-local config automatically.
App initializes node-llama-cpp for the selected model, performs a readiness check, then marks the model as ready.
The model becomes usable in the existing LLM flow without further setup.
userJourney.emptyStateCopy: Choose a recommended local model and click Add & Download to start using local AI.

genericModelListRules.summary: Rules for how managed-local models appear in the generic (all models) list.
genericModelListRules.listDisplay: Show 'Local Model' badge + model name + running status. Never show endpoint URL.
genericModelListRules.editAction: Redirect to the dedicated Local Models page. Do not open the generic edit form.
genericModelListRules.enableDisable: Normal toggle, same as remote models.
genericModelListRules.delete: Redirect to the dedicated Local Models page for the uninstall flow.
genericModelListRules.testConnection: Performed automatically via the runtime manager readiness check. No URL shown to user.

preflightChecks: Block the action when free disk space is lower than the required download size plus a safety buffer.
Show a simple resource warning when the larger model may exceed available memory, while recommending the smaller model instead.
Use the bundled node-llama-cpp runtime that matches the packaged app build automatically.
Resume interrupted downloads automatically whenever the source supports ranged requests.

autoSelection.defaultQuantizationStrategy: One verified recommended quantization per model. Normal users never choose quantization.
autoSelection.modelRecommendationStrategy: Qwen3.5 4B as the default recommended option for most devices. Qwen3.5 9B as the higher-quality option when hardware allows.
autoSelection.fallbackPolicy: If the primary repository is unavailable, switch to a verified fallback repository without changing the UI flow.

autoConfiguration: Managed local models never ask for protocol, endpoint, API key, or model identifier.
The app stores an internal installedArtifactId and derives all connection details from it.
The app creates a managed-local LLM config immediately after installation succeeds.
Only one managed local runtime stays active at a time; switching models stops the previous one automatically.
autoRecovery: Retry transient network failures with backoff.
Preserve partial downloads so they can resume after app restart.
If runtime startup fails, keep the installation and expose one-click retry.
If checksum verification fails, delete the corrupted artifact and restart the download from a clean state.

hiddenFromNormalUsers: localhost IP address and port number
defaultPostInstallBehavior: Create the managed-local model entry automatically after installation.
Start the runtime automatically after installation unless the user has disabled auto-run globally.
If no model is active yet, make the new local model active automatically.
If the model is already installed, replace the primary action with Start or Use Now.

advancedMode.entry: Only behind an explicit Advanced action.

requirements: Use temporary .part files until checksum verification succeeds.
Preflight disk-space checks before starting a download.
Limit concurrent large downloads to keep the app responsive.
Emit progress events from the main process over IPC.

startupFlow: Ensure the selected GGUF model is installed.
Ensure the bundled node-llama-cpp runtime is available for the current platform.
Load the selected GGUF file through node-llama-cpp.
Create the managed context and chat session with system defaults.
Complete the runtime readiness path before exposing the model as available.
shutdownFlow: Stop the active local runtime when the user switches to another local model.
Stop the active local runtime on app quit.
Preserve logs and last health status for troubleshooting.

registryEntities.installedArtifact: Tracks downloaded GGUF model files and the managed runtime metadata associated with them.
registryEntities.managedLocalConfig: Links a user-visible local model entry (configType: managed-local) to an installedArtifactId. No user-editable endpoint or API key stored.
registryEntities.activeRuntime: Tracks the single running node-llama-cpp model/context/session lifecycle.

edgeCases.insufficientDisk: Block the action and tell the user how much additional free space is needed.
edgeCases.insufficientMemory: Recommend the smaller model instead of exposing low-level tuning first.
edgeCases.reinstall: If the same model is already installed, replace the primary action with Start or Use Now.
edgeCases.switchModel: Switching active local models stops the previous runtime automatically.

rollout: Phase 1: artifact registry, download queue, runtime package installation, managed-local config type, and zero-config binding primitives.
Phase 2: dedicated one-click local model catalog UI with Qwen3.5 4B and 9B download entries.
Phase 3: managed llama.cpp start/stop, health checks, seamless activation, and auto-recovery.
Phase 4: advanced mode, diagnostics, llamacpp type deprioritized to advanced section, more models.
